outcome: rate of Premature Rupture of Membranes (PROM)
cohort: 151 pregnant women between 37 and 42 weeks of gestational age treated at Rasoul Akram Hospital in Iran.
finding: Transvaginal sonography of cervical length (CL) and cervical angle (CA) demonstrated adequate diagnostic accuracy in predicting spontaneous birth, need for labor induction, cesarean delivery, and incidence of PROM in full-term pregnant women.
mod_finding: Cervical length (CL) of 21 mm predicted cesarean delivery with 72.2% sensitivity and 79.1% specificity, and a cervical angle (CA) of 115.2 degrees showed 70.3% sensitivity and 78.4% specificity for predicting vaginal delivery.
